drivingQuestion: Does a fetus that died inside its mother's womb impart carcass impurity to one who touches it there?
outcomeNote: A mishna stating a rule and one named tanna's dissent; nothing is argued or decided here.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּהֵמָה שֶׁמֵּת עוּבָּרָהּ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעֶיהָ וְהוֹשִׁיט הָרוֹעֶה אֶת יָדוֹ וְנָגַע בּוֹ, בֵּין בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה בֵּין בִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה – טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: בִּטְמֵאָה – טָמֵא, וּבִטְהוֹרָה – טָהוֹר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «an animal whose fetus died in its womb and the shepherd reached his hand» into the womb «and touched» the fetus, «both in» the case of «a non-kosher animal and in» the case of «a kosher animal» the fetus does not have the status of an animal carcass that imparts ritual impurity, and the shepherd remains «ritually pure. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: In» the case of «a non-kosher» animal it is «impure, and in» the case of «a kosher» animal it is «pure.»

moves.summary: the first tanna rules the shepherd pure in both a kosher and a non-kosher animal
moves.about: whether a shepherd who reaches into a womb and touches a fetus that died there contracts carcass impurity — the first tanna rules him pure in every case, R׳ Yosei HaGelili only in a kosher animal

moves.summary: R׳ Yosei HaGelili distinguishes: impure in a non-kosher animal, pure in a kosher one

edges.cueHe: רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר: בטמאה – טמא, ובטהורה – טהור
